introduction.text: Fontana dei Quattro Fiumi, the Fountain of the Four Rivers, is a Baroque fountain in Rome’s Piazza Navona. Designed by Gian Lorenzo Bernini in 1651 for Pope Innocent X, it symbolizes papal authority across the four continents and remains a key example of Baroque sculpture and urban waterworks.

design.description: Bernini’s design features a travertine basin supporting four river‑god statues and a Roman copy of an Egyptian obelisk topped with the Pamphili family dove emblem.

art.description: The fountain’s allegorical river gods—Nile, Danube, Ganges, and Río de la Plata—are sculpted in naturalistic style, each carrying symbolic attributes that reflect their respective continents.
